source_caption:
🎬 Click (2006)

Click follows Michael Newman, a hardworking architect struggling to balance his demanding career with his responsibilities as a husband and father. His life changes when he discovers a mysterious universal remote control that allows him to pause, rewind, fast-forward, and control moments in his life. At first, Michael uses the device to skip arguments, boring conversations, and everyday frustrations, believing it will make his life easier. However, as the remote begins making decisions on its own, he realizes that skipping life’s difficult moments also means missing precious memories with the people he loves. Combining hilarious comedy, emotional storytelling, and unexpected life lessons, the film explores family, love, regret, and the importance of appreciating every moment.

🎭 Genre: Comedy • Drama • Fantasy • Romance

⭐ IMDb: 6.4/10

⏱️ Runtime: 1h 47m • PG-13

🎥 Director: Frank Coraci

🏆 Recognition: Starring Adam Sandler, Kate Beckinsale, Christopher Walken, and David Hasselhoff, the film received an Academy Award nomination for Best Makeup and is remembered for its surprising emotional depth.

source_details.synopsis: Click is a 2006 American fantasy comedy-drama film directed by Frank Coraci, written by Steve Koren and Mark O'Keefe, both of whom produced with Jack Giarraputo, Neal H. Moritz, and Adam Sandler, who also starred in the lead role. The film co-stars Kate Beckinsale, Christopher Walken, Henry Winkler, David Hasselhoff, Julie Kavner, and Sean Astin. Sandler plays Michael Newman, a workaholic family man and architect who acquires a magical universal remote that enables him to control reality. The film is inspired by "The Magic Thread", a folk tale included in The Book of Virtues: A Treasury of Great Moral Stories. Filming began in late 2005 and was finished by early 2006. Sony Pictures Releasing
